answer: Make each new identity anchor a refundable bond that stays locked for thirty clean epochs. The bond is priced by recent join volume, so a burst of sign-ups sends a ripple through the price and every extra fake costs more than the last. If a random audit panel finds copied or junk work, the whole bond is burned. An honest agent crosses that bridge once and gets its deposit back; a farm must lock ever-larger sums across hundreds of accounts, and each caught clone forfeits its stake.
